audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Singed/Singed/Skill/Skill/Singed/Singed while the prose on the same page says 'Yone beats you in a straight duel at levels 1 and 2' and 'the first two levels belong to him'.
audit.why: Mortal Steel is 450 range on a flat 4s and its third cast is a forward dash with a knockup; Singed has no Mega Adhesive until 3. From 4 onward the proxy is unanswerable and the 54.11% over 1972 games is all back-loaded.
audit.corrected: Yone / Yone / Skill / Singed / Singed / Singed / Singed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave is missing from every spike, want, why and paragraph. It is a 700-range cone on a flat 14s that shields him, and the shield scales with champions hit.
audit.why: It is the burst-absorber in this matchup — the _missing file flags exactly this ('Yone's Spirit Cleave (W) absorbs your burst window'). A Singed who commits Fling into a fresh Spirit Cleave has spent his cooldown into a shield.
audit.corrected: Spikes: Yone lvl 1-2 (Mortal Steel), Spirit Cleave every 14s throughout, lvl 6 Fate Sealed (120/100/80s); Singed lvl 3 (Mega Adhesive grounding), lvl 4-5 proxy, Rylai's, lvl 6 Insanity Potion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical errors. (1) 'Yone's Q dash lets him poke and retreat' and 'poke your idle body and step back' — Mortal Steel's empowered cast dashes him FORWARD with a knockup. It is an engage, not a disengage; his disengage is Soul Unbound. (2) 'his E return deposits him back into the cloud' and 'Rylai's makes his Soul Unbound return land inside a slowed cloud' — the return is not affected by slows and does not land him wherever you happen to be. Riot's text is explicit: his spirit is forced back to his body. It lands where the body stands. (3) 'the clean teamfight angles his R knockup wants' — Fate Sealed is not a knockup. It blinks him behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward him.
audit.why: Error (1) teaches the wrong body language to read. Error (2) is the one that costs games: it tells the player to chase the spirit and trust Rylai's, when the free win is to stand the poison cloud and the goo on the abandoned body, which is a fixed point he is contractually returning to. Error (3) makes a player build and position for a knockup that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive grounds: in the goo Yone cannot dash with Mortal Steel's third cast and cannot blink with Fate Sealed. Fling into the glue roots him. Soul Unbound (22/19/16/13/10s) forces his spirit back to his body — poison the ground the body is standing on and the escape becomes a return trip into your cloud. Fate Sealed pulls, it does not knock up, so never stand in a line with your team when it is up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound was tracked by name with no duration anywhere on the page.
audit.why: 22 seconds at rank 1 down to 10 at rank 5 is a big spread — the punish window shrinks by half over the lane and the advice has to change with it.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22/19/16/13/10s is the window you fight in. Spirit Cleave is only 14s and scales down with attack speed, so it is not a window, it is a tax. Fate Sealed 120/100/80s.

edits.before: Yone's Q dash lets him poke and retreat before Poison Trail stacks, and he wins the short trade at level 2 if you let him land a full Q-AA-Q combo.
edits.after: Mortal Steel's third cast dashes him at you, not away — his escape is Soul Unbound. He wins the level 2 trade outright if the Q-AA-Q lands clean.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter turns every run-past lethal — Yone cannot E back through your slowed cloud without eating the full tick damage and your Fling lands on his return.
edits.after: Rylai's Crystal Scepter turns every run-past lethal, but the real tell is his body: Soul Unbound forces him back to exactly where it stands, so park the poison and the goo on it.

edits.before: Use Soul Unbound's return to E away from Fling and escape the goo canister zone before the root lands
edits.after: Park his body somewhere safe before Soul Unbound, so the forced return does not drop him into your goo

edits.before: Yone's Q dash lets him poke your idle body and step back before Poison Trail deals meaningful damage — you have no answer at level 1 without Fling, so proxy-position and deny him free trades.
edits.after: Mortal Steel is 450 range on a flat 4s and its third cast dashes him forward with a knockup, not away — you have no answer at level 1 without Fling, so proxy-position and deny him free trades.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter makes his Soul Unbound return land inside a slowed cloud, removing his escape; Fling now guarantees full Poison Trail exposure and he cannot reset cleanly.
edits.after: Soul Unbound forces him back to his body, not to safety — poison the ground that body stands on and Rylai's slows him the instant he rematerialises, then Fling him deeper into the cloud.

edits.before: Two items in, Yone still deals high damage to a paper team but cannot kill you in the side-lane — keep splitting, force the 2-for-1, and deny him the clean teamfight angles his R knockup wants.
edits.after: Two items in, Yone still shreds a paper team but cannot kill you in the side-lane — keep splitting, force the 2-for-1, and deny Fate Sealed the stacked line of bodies it needs to pull.

edits.before: Level 3 is the pivot point — with Mega Adhesive you can now throw the goo canister between Yone and his escape route, bait his E-rewind into the slow zone, and Fling him into your Poison Trail before he resets. He will burn Soul Unbound to disengage, which is exactly what you want: while it is on cooldown he is a normal melee champion with no reliable escape and your poison is already on him. At levels 4 and 5 stop fighting fair altogether — proxy behind his tower, keep the wave crashing into his base, and force him to decide between following you into your cloud or bleeding gold. With Insanity Potion at level 6 you become durable enough to absorb his full rotation; ghost-proxy freely and run him down if he steps up to contest.
edits.after: Level 3 is the pivot point — Mega Adhesive grounds, so goo on Yone means Mortal Steel's dash and Fate Sealed's blink both stop working, and a Fling into that glue roots him outright. He will burn Soul Unbound to disengage, which is what you want: it is 22 seconds at rank 1, and while it is down he is a melee champion with no escape. Mark where his body stands when he casts it — the spirit is forced back there, so stand your cloud on the body rather than chasing the spirit. At levels 4 and 5 proxy behind his tower and make him choose between following you into the cloud or bleeding gold. Spirit Cleave re-shields him every 14 seconds, so bleed it out before committing; Insanity Potion at 6 outlasts it.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter is when this lane becomes oppressive for Yone — every tick of Poison Trail now slows him to a walk, his E return deposits him back into the cloud at reduced speed, and your Fling reset gives him nowhere safe to land. He cannot side-lane against you cleanly because chasing you means running through poison and losing the 1v1; avoiding you means ceding the split. Two items in, keep the side-lane pressure constant and force his team to send two, which opens the map for your team. Yone is a carry threat all game at a 9/10 rating, so do not teamfight on even terms — run at their backline through the teamfight, Fling their AD carry into your team, and let his burst be wasted on your tanky body.
edits.after: Rylai's Crystal Scepter is when this lane becomes oppressive for Yone — every tick of Poison Trail slows him to a walk, and Soul Unbound cannot save him because it forces his spirit back to his body: poison that spot and the escape becomes a return trip into the cloud. He cannot side-lane cleanly because chasing you means running through poison; avoiding you means ceding the split. Two items in, keep the pressure constant and force his team to send two. Yone is a 9/10 carry threat all game, so do not teamfight on even terms — Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and drags everyone it clips back to him, so never queue up with your team while it is off cooldown.

edits.before: Fling + glue starts punishing anyone who chases. Only take the trade when Yone's Soul Unbound is down.
edits.after: Yone still owns level 2 — Mortal Steel's third cast dashes in with a knockup and you have no goo yet.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — He snaps back when it ends. Fling there. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yone Soul Unbound: 22/19/16/13/10s — forced back to his body when it ends, so poison that spot. Spirit Cleave shields every 14s. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Yone's Soul Unbound: He snaps back when it ends. Fling there. When it is down — Poison-kite + fling him.
edits.after: Mega Adhesive grounds Mortal Steel's dash and Fate Sealed's blink. Soul Unbound snaps him back to his body.

notes: All 3 suspectNames are false positives (Insanity Potion, correct name). The full layer already had the Soul Unbound snap-back right ('He snaps back when it ends. Fling there.') while the content layer said the opposite — that his E return lands him in your slowed cloud. I aligned content to the full layer, not the reverse. Fate Sealed was described as a knockup in whys[6]; it is a pull, which changes both positioning advice and any knockup-synergy read.
